task.description: Step 2b (design gate) of WF-03 for ISS-0418. Independently verify CODE-DESIGNER's design against the six numbered checks in this run's dispatch (lease placement outside the kill boundary, monitor backstop correctness, default-cap protectiveness, wasm_hang determinism claim, new-primitive justification, honesty audit).

result.summary:
FAIL. One BLOCKER and one MAJOR finding, both concrete and independently re-derived against real source, not the design's own narrative.

=== CHECK-BY-CHECK ===

1. LEASE PLACEMENT (design §2/§8.1). PASS on its own terms. Traced plugin_interface.ex's real invoke/2,3: it spawns the killable task via Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 and the caller of invoke/2,3 is a DIFFERENT, never-killed process (Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) targets only the inner async_nolink task, confirmed by reading handle_yield_result's nil clause at plugin_interface.ex). So 'acquire in invoke/2,3's caller, before calling invoke/2,3 at all' is a correct placement outside the kill boundary, and §8.1's self-correction (striking the original handle_node/1 placement, which DOES run inside the killed task) is real and necessary -- confirmed by reading plugin_handler.ex's handle_node/1, which does run as the body of the async_nolink'd fn. No blocker here on placement reasoning itself.

   HOWEVER, this placement is only correct for a caller that does not yet exist (see finding 1 below) -- the abstract reasoning is sound but has no shipped instantiation.

2. MONITOR BACKSTOP (design §2, §5.3, §5.4). PASS on substance, MINOR citation defect. The demonitor+flush-on-explicit-release / DOWN-scan-on-crash pattern is specified concretely enough to build (state shape §5.3, handle_call/handle_info behavior §5.4 prose) and cannot double-release: an explicit release/1 removes the leases entry and demonitors+flushes BEFORE any queued stale :DOWN can be processed (mirrors the real pollers_breaker.ex handle_info clause I read, which ignores a :DOWN whose ref no longer matches current state -- same shape). The SandboxPool citations are directionally accurate (Process.monitor(owner_pid) in reserve_slot, and a flush-before-classify demonitor in the {ref, result} handle_info clause, both real idioms in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex) but the specific line numbers are off: reserve_slot's Process.monitor(owner_pid) is at sandbox_pool.ex:566, not the cited :567; the demonitor+flush is at :407 inside the {ref, result} clause context, not the cited :406. This is a precision nit only -- the pattern cited is real and present -- but naming it since a design that cites line numbers should get them right, and a future reader trusting the citation blind gets sent one line off.

3. DEFAULT CAP PROTECTIVENESS (design §5.5) -- MAJOR FINDING, not merely a nitpick. Computed both hosts as instructed:
   - CI runner (ubuntu-latest, ~4 vCPU per ISS-0418's own recurrence evidence): schedulers_online ~4 -> default cap = max(4-2,1) = 2. Native pool (available_parallelism, typically tracks vCPU 1:1 on a dedicated runner) ~4. Cap (2) < pool (~4): protective on this host.
   - This workstation, using the design's OWN cited numbers (§5.5 itself quotes REQ-170 §1.5's measurement: available_parallelism()=8, System.schedulers_online()=16, confirmed again live via `nproc`=16 in this session -- note ISSUE-FIXER's OWN diagnosis measured both at 16 on ITS reproduction host, i.e. the design is citing REQ-170's host, not ISSUE-FIXER's, for the divergent numbers): default cap = max(16-2,1) = 14. Native pool = 8 (per the design's own cited figure). 14 > 8: THE DEFAULT CAP EXCEEDS THE ACTUAL NATIVE POOL SIZE ON A HOST THE DESIGN ITSELF USES AS ITS WORKED EXAMPLE. Per the design's own stated rule three paragraphs earlier in the same section ("a cap at or above the actual native pool size permits exactly the same worst case as no cap"), this default is a NO-OP exactly on the host it uses to justify the headroom formula. The design's closing claim in §5.5 ("guarantees the cap is strictly below the proxy count on every host this formula runs on") is true only for schedulers_online() itself (16-2=14<16) -- it silently substitutes "the proxy count" for "the actual pool size" in the sentence that matters, and does not run its own formula against the divergent case it just finished quoting. This is a design-internal contradiction against the design's own evidence, not a hypothetical edge case: it is proven using only numbers already inside the document.

4. WASM_HANG DETERMINISM CLAIM (design §6/§6.1/§6.2) -- BLOCKER, and the most serious finding, because it is the claim the whole run is justified by. Read the real wasm_hang-tagged tests directly (test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs:152,353,393,472; call_timeout_test.exs:76,155; host_api_write_test.exs:458). EVERY one of them calls `PluginInterface.invoke(PluginHandler, hang_context, ...)` or `PluginHandler.handle_node(...)` DIRECTLY from the test process -- the test itself is 'the caller of PluginInterface.invoke/2,3' that §8.1 identifies as the correct lease-acquisition point. But §1 and §8.1 both explicitly forbid modifying PluginInterface.invoke/2,3, PluginHandler, or handle_node/1 (§8.1: 'PluginHandler needs no change at all'; §1: 'does NOT touch PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's crash-safety algorithm'). §8.1 defers the actual lease-acquiring call site to 'whichever future requirement builds runtime dispatch' (OQ-C), which 'does not exist yet in the shipped codebase today.' §6.2 confirms the existing wasm_hang tests are 'NOT rewritten to assert on InvocationLease directly' and specifies no rewrite of them to CALL try_acquire/release either. The net result: there is no code path, anywhere this design specifies building, by which an existing wasm_hang test (or anything in its call graph) ever calls InvocationLease.try_acquire/0. A cap: 1 override on a GenServer nothing in the request path ever calls cannot admit anything 'one at a time' -- it does not participate in the request path at all. §6.1's claim ('within that isolated subprocess, hangs are admitted ONE AT A TIME by construction, never concurrently, regardless of runner size or contention' and 'a test that cannot begin dispatching until the previous invocation's lease is held cannot race that previous invocation for pool slots, full stop, by construction') is FALSE as applied to the actual, currently-flaking tests, given this design's own scope decisions. The design does not merely fail to fully fix the flake (which would be acceptable, per this gate's brief, if honestly stated) -- it affirmatively claims a structural guarantee ('not left to chance', 'this is not hope it stops flaking') that its own §1/§8.1 scope boundary makes impossible to realize without an as-yet-unbuilt, unspecified change to the wasm_hang tests themselves or to invoke/2,3/PluginHandler (both of which the design forbids touching). This is exactly the overclaim the dispatch's honesty-audit item (6) was watching for, in the one section the dispatch flagged as 'most worth attacking, because it is what the whole run is justified by.'

5. NEW-PRIMITIVE DECISION (design §3). PASS. The four grounds (caller-cooperation mismatch with Admission's documented crash semantics; capacity-vs-blast-radius exhaustion-shape mismatch; no per-tenant partition on the underlying native resource; sidesteps ISS-0437 by having no tenant-keyed map at all) each independently hold against the real admission.ex moduledoc I read in full -- its own 'Crash / restart semantics' section states verbatim that it does not monitor callers and a leaked ref stays counted until explicit release or a server restart, confirming ground (a) is not fabricated. Ground (d)'s ISS-0437 sidestep is real: InvocationLease's state (§5.3) has no tenant-keyed structure of any kind, so ISS-0437's per-tenant-entry retention gap has no analogue here by construction, not by assertion.

6. HONESTY AUDIT (design §0, §7, moduledoc mandate). MIXED. §0 and §7's moduledoc-mandated text are genuinely honest and precisely scoped -- the 'bounds concurrent callers, not leaked threads' distinction is stated plainly, repeatedly, and matches ISSUE-FIXER's live-reproduced finding exactly; nothing in §0/§7 overclaims what the cap prevents regarding the native leak itself, and this is the outcome the dispatch wanted confirmed where true, so it is confirmed here for §0/§7 specifically. §4's reclamation-scoping is likewise honest and consistent. But §6/§6.1's determinism claim (finding 2 above) IS an overclaim, and it is not confined to sloppy wording -- §6.2 supplies the exact fact (tests not rewritten) that refutes §6.1's own conclusion in the same section, meaning the contradiction is visible on a straight read of the document's own two adjacent subsections, not something requiring outside evidence to catch (though outside evidence -- reading the real test files -- is what this validation used to confirm it conclusively).

=== VERDICT ===
FAIL. Two findings below; the first is a BLOCKER on its own (WF-02 Step 1b: fail immediately and completely on any single failed check, no partial credit). Route back to CODE-DESIGNER.

issues.finding: The design claims (§6.1) that a cap:1 test-environment override makes wasm_hang admission 'structurally impossible... by construction, not probabilistic,' but every real :wasm_hang-tagged test (test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs:152,353,393,472; call_timeout_test.exs:76,155; host_api_write_test.exs:458) calls PluginInterface.invoke/2,3 or PluginHandler.handle_node/1 directly from the test process, and the design's own §1/§8.1 forbid modifying PluginInterface.invoke/2,3, PluginHandler, or handle_node/1 -- deferring the only specified lease-acquiring call site to a future, unbuilt dispatch-integration requirement (OQ-C). §6.2 confirms the existing wasm_hang tests are not rewritten to call try_acquire/release either. Net effect: nothing in any code path this design specifies building ever calls InvocationLease.try_acquire/0 or release/1 from the actual flaking tests' call graph, so the cap cannot gate their admission at all -- §6.1's determinism claim is false as applied to the tests it is offered to fix. Required fix: either (a) specify the exact call site/wrapper the wasm_hang tests (or a helper they're changed to use) call to acquire/release the lease around their own invoke/handle_node calls, with that wrapper's own crash-safety reasoning re-derived (since a test-side wrapper is a different call shape than production dispatch), or (b) drop the determinism claim entirely and restate §6 honestly as 'this design does not yet fix the CI flake; it specifies a contract a future dispatch-integration call site must follow, and the flake persists until that caller exists and is wired into the wasm_hang tests' own paths.' Option (b) would still need CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-review only for the changed §6 text and its consistency with §0/§7 (a scope-shrink, not new design work), but it is a materially different design conclusion than what CODE-DESIGNER's own step-02 handoff claims to ORCH ('the fix is made DETERMINISTIC... within the isolated mix test --only wasm_hang subprocess').

The recommended default cap, max(System.schedulers_online() - 2, 1), computed against the design's own cited figures (available_parallelism()=8, schedulers_online()=16, both quoted in this same section from REQ-170 §1.5 and re-confirmed live this session via `nproc`=16) yields a default of 14 -- which exceeds the actual native pool size (8) on that exact host. Per the design's own stated rule earlier in the identical section ('a cap at or above the actual native pool size permits exactly the same worst case as no cap'), the recommended default is a no-op on the host the design itself uses as its worked numeric example, contradicting its own closing claim that the formula 'guarantees the cap is strictly below the proxy count on every host this formula runs on' (true only if 'the proxy count' silently means schedulers_online() itself rather than the actual pool size the guarantee needs to bind). On a smaller CI runner (~4 vCPU) the same formula does protect (cap 2 vs pool ~4), so this is not uniformly broken, but the design ships an OQ (OQ-B) leaving the exact formula to ELIXIR-DEV without flagging that its OWN recommended starting point fails on a real, already-measured host. Required fix: either derive the default from available_parallelism() itself (if reachable from Elixir via :erlang.system_info or a similar BEAM-side call -- not investigated by this design) or state explicitly, next to the formula, that operators on hosts where schedulers_online() significantly exceeds the actual wasmex pool size (BEAM scheduler count set higher than physical/logical cores, e.g. via +S) must override the default manually, since the formula's own proxy assumption can silently fail to protect -- currently only a soft caveat exists ('not because the two are guaranteed equal') without stating the concrete consequence (a non-protective default) plainly.

next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (rework) to fix the BLOCKER (§6 determinism claim vs. §1/§8.1 scope boundary) and the MAJOR (§5.5 default-cap formula's own worked example showing non-protection). Re-submit to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a fresh gate pass once revised -- do not re-approve without re-reading the revised §5.5/§6 in full.
